 Judgment

The appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 07.04.2011 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Haveri, in MVC No.305/2009, calling in question dismissal of the claim petition.

sentences.text: 2. It is the case of the claimant that on 23.12.2007 at about 12 noon the claimant was sitting in front of house of one Iranna Prasadimath.

At that time a driver of the truck bearing registration No.KA-27/TA-1264 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner dashed the claimant,
due to which, the claimant has sustained injuries and immediately he was shifted to the Ayurvedic treatment at Bagali and thereafter he was referred to KIMS hospital, Hubballi.
The tribunal has dismissed the claim petition on the ground that there is a delay of two months in lodging the complaint to the police.
Therefore, the claimant is in appeal.
Heard arguments from both sides and perused the materials placed before the Court.
4. It is proved that the accident was caused on 23.12.2007 and complaint was lodged on 09.02.2008.
Therefore, there is nearly two months in lodging the complaint before police.
It is natural that consequential spot panchanama was conducted and charge sheet is filed.

Therefore,
these police documents cannot prove the injury sustained by the claimant in the accident.
But at earliest point of time regarding the accident and injury sustained, what the claimant did is to be considered and appreciated.
It is stated that initially the claimant was admitted to the hospital for Ayurvedic treatment at Bagali.
Thereafter on 25.12.2007 the claimant was admitted in KIMS hospital, Hubballi.
Ex.P.5 is the wound certificate.
Ex.P.7, P.8, P.25 and P.27 are discharge cards which prove that the claimant was admitted to the KIMS hospital which extracts road traffic accident occurred on 23.12.2007.
Therefore, these medical evidences are to be considered.

PW.2 is the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13263 doctor working in KIMS Hospital and he has stated that the claimant Shivayya S/O Gadigayya Prasadimath vs Shivappa S/O Siddappa Kaginelli on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118744197/
2 was admitted in the hospital in road traffic accident.
Therefore, even through there is delay of nearly two months in lodging complaint but that is for the reasons explained in the complaint.
There was compromise talks between driver/owner and claimed that claimant was assured to get reimbursement of medical expenses, but it was not materialised.
Therefore, lodged complaint before the police, but the medical evidence on record prove that the claimant had sustained injuries in the motor vehicle accident and had admitted to the hospital.

Therefore, just because there is delay in lodging the complaint cannot be a ground to reject the claim petition in view of principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ravi vs. Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 Supreme Court Cases 693.

sentences.text: Therefore, dismissal of the claim petition by the tribunal is hereby set aside.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, a compensation of Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering.
Further, a compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
6. The claimant has sustained fracture to the right thigh.
The claimant is a driver by profession.
The doctor had stated that the claimant has suffered physical disability towards whole body at 10% and therefore, this is taken as a functional disability.
The accident is caused in the year 2007.

Therefore,
notional income of Rs.4,000/- per month is taken into consideration, which is recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The claimant was aged 27 years at the time of accident.
Therefore appropriate applicable multiplier is 17.

Hence, loss of future income due to disability is hereby reassessed and quantified as Rs.81,600/- (Rs.4,000 x 10% x 12 x 17).
7.
The compensation awarded towards medical expenses and hospital charges of Rs.38,304/- is as per NC: 2023:KHC-D:13263 Ex.P.28, 29, 48 to 80 which are the actual bills and receipts produced.
Therefore, the same is kept intact.
Further, a compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards incidental expenses like food, nourishment, traveling, attendant charges, etc.,.
Further, a compensation of Rs.8,000/- is awarded under the head loss of income during laid up period for a period of two months.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads.

Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards injuries, pain and 30,000  suffering.
2. Towards medical expenses.
38,304  3. Towards loss of amenities.

25,000  4. Towards loss of income during 8,000  laid up period and medical  treatment period.
 5. Towards incidental charges like 10,000 Shivayya S/O Gadigayya Prasadimath vs Shivappa S/O Siddappa Kaginelli on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118744197/
3  attendant charges, food,

 6. Towards loss of future earning 81,600  capacity.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,92,904/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

9. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 07.04.2011 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Haveri, in MVC No.305/2009 is hereby set aside.
iii) The claimant is entitled total compensation of Rs.1,92,904/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
